journal_text: In Blackrose the Chainbreakers keep a house, the one with the carved post of broken chains by its door. I'm to hear Never-Sold out about a woman on an estate north of the town, and make her trust me with it.
directions: The Chainbreakers' house is in Blackrose, the door with the carved post of broken chains beside it, on the town's east side.

journal_text: Never-Sold told me of Rows-For-Another, who took a boat from an estate on the swamp road north of Blackrose on four months' work, eleven years ago, and works it still. Never-Sold has put by enough to buy out what it was. I'm to meet her at the estate's landing north of the town, press the steward Hulm-Tei to name the buy-out, and then choose with Rows-For-Another how she leaves.
directions: From Blackrose take the swamp road north out of the town; the estate's landing is a short walk on, on the channel side, with a work shed and boats at the water.

journal_text: Hulm-Tei's book is true at every line, and by it Rows-For-Another owes more now than when she took the boat. Never-Sold wants the book itself. I'm to take the debt book from the chest in the work shed on the estate landing, unseen, and bring it to Never-Sold at the landing.
directions: The work shed is the low shed at the landing's edge, by the boats; the chest is inside on the left.

journal_text: I took Hulm-Tei's debt book from the work shed on the estate landing. Never-Sold read it through and found where its true lines grow the Owing. I'm to put the book before Hulm-Tei at the landing and bring the buy-out down to what Rows-For-Another first owed.
directions: Hulm-Tei stands at the landing by day, by the work shed.

journal_text: Rows-For-Another will not wait on Hulm-Tei's book. At night two estate men walk the estate landing north of Blackrose, and the channel runs from the landing out of the estate's reach; she cannot drown in it. I'm to come back after dark, keep the two men off her unseen, and swim the channel with her to where it leaves the estate.
directions: The channel runs past the landing's boats north-east, away from the road; where it leaves the estate it passes under a fallen trunk.

journal_text: I put Hulm-Tei's own book before him at the estate landing north of Blackrose, and its true lines brought Rows-For-Another's buy-out down to what she first owed. Never-Sold paid it. Rows-For-Another walks off the swamp road free, without her boat.

After dark I kept the two estate men off Rows-For-Another on the landing north of Blackrose and swam the channel with her until it left the estate. She is free and gone, and can never go back to the swamp road. Never-Sold says the estate will be harder on the next one it holds.
Never-Sold sent word from the Chainbreakers' house in Blackrose that she has need of me. I'm to go to the house, the door with the carved post of broken chains beside it, and hear her (Speechcraft).
directions: The Chainbreakers' house is in Blackrose, the door with the carved post of broken chains beside it.

journal_text: The cells under the Rose's outer post at Blackrose's edge are burning, and three the heirs hold are inside, Rows-For-Another's mother among them. The heirs' gate-keepers will not go in. I'm to get through the stockade gate at the outer post, by talking Third-Born Tsaxi round or slipping past, and go down into the cells.
directions: The outer post is at the town's south edge, where the stockade of stakes stands round a low door, under BM&V's 'Black Rose Jail' marker; smoke shows it from the town.

journal_text: Inside the burning cells under the outer post three are held, each reached its own way. Says-It-Plain is behind a lock; Hides-In-Reeds is up a collapsed way; Keeps-The-Old-Count is in the flooded cell. When the first is out the way burns shut. I'm to reach one of them and tell them to come with me.
directions: From the door the passage forks three ways in the smoke; the locked cell is straight on, the collapsed way climbs on the left, and the flooded cell is down the steps on the right.

journal_text: The timber over the passage fell as the first of them came to me, and the way in is shut by fire; the other two are beyond it. The flooded cell's drain still runs out to the gate square. I'm to swim the drain with the one I reached and bring them out to the gate square of the outer post.
directions: The drain opens in the floor of the flooded cell, down the steps on the right of the fork, and runs out under the stockade to the gate square.

journal_text: I brought Says-It-Plain out of the burning cells under the Rose's outer post by the flooded drain. The other two died in the fire. He spoke their names to Never-Sold at the Chainbreakers' house, and she keeps them.

I brought Hides-In-Reeds out of the burning cells under the Rose's outer post by the flooded drain. The other two died in the fire. She does not deny her killing. She spoke their names to Never-Sold at the Chainbreakers' house, and she keeps them.

I brought Keeps-The-Old-Count, Rows-For-Another's mother, out of the burning cells under the Rose's outer post by the flooded drain. The other two died in the fire. She spoke their names to Never-Sold at the Chainbreakers' house, and she keeps them.
Nobody came out of the burning cells under the Rose's outer post. Never-Sold at the Chainbreakers' house keeps the three names herself.

On Soulrest's open dock the broker Ussa-Rekh, who bought out Owings for thirty years, refused Heavy-Rope's crew their last season. The crew know me as the Chainbreakers'. I'm to hear Ussa-Rekh and Heavy-Rope on the dock and take one side (Speechcraft).
directions: Soulrest's open dock is the long dock on the town's water, where the crews wait for hire; Ussa-Rekh's cabin stands on it.

journal_text: I stood with Heavy-Rope's crew on Soulrest's open dock. Ussa-Rekh keeps their carved tokens in a chest in his cabin on the dock, and a crew that breaks its tokens before him is done with him. I'm to pick the chest's lock in his cabin (Lockpicking), take the tokens unseen (Sneak) and give them to Heavy-Rope.
directions: Ussa-Rekh's cabin is the small cabin at the dock's end; the chest is inside under the window.

journal_text: I stood with Ussa-Rekh on Soulrest's open dock. Heavy-Rope will not take the refusal from a stranger's mouth and wants it settled with fists. I'm to face Heavy-Rope in a brawl on the dock and win it (Block, and the fists).
directions: Heavy-Rope waits for the player at the middle of the dock, among his crew.

journal_text: I took the crew's tokens from Ussa-Rekh's cabin on Soulrest's open dock and gave them to Heavy-Rope, and the crew broke them before Ussa-Rekh. They are done with him a season early, and he will hire neither them nor me again.
I beat Heavy-Rope in a brawl on Soulrest's open dock, standing with Ussa-Rekh. The crew will work their last season, and lose their trade on the dock after it.

I came to Claywater Station on the Blackwood Road. Travellers there pay Livia Varinius, the well-keeper, 2 drakes for the stop this season. Signs-For-The-Cargo, the landing's poler, now wants 1 drake from every walker who wades the ford. I'm to hear each keeper's side. Claywater Station is about 640 yards west of the signpost at Cartwright's Cross on the Blackwood Road, where the arms point to Gideon and to Leyawiin. Going west, a painted pole barrier stands in a field about 110 yards off the road on the right; that is the Drowning Gate. The station house roof shows about 100 yards on, ahead on the left. Livia Varinius keeps the well at the station house door, inside the low stone walls. Signs-For-The-Cargo poles the plank raft at the landing stage across the ford in the morning, about 65 yards north of the well. The round mud huts stand behind it on the far bank. If the road runs on into open marsh with no roofs in sight, I have passed it.
directions: From the Blackwood Road: Claywater Station is about 640 yards west of the signpost at Cartwright's Cross, where the arms point to Gideon and to Leyawiin. Going west, a painted pole barrier stands in a field about 110 yards off the road on the right; that is the Drowning Gate, and the station house roof shows about 100 yards on, ahead on the left. The well stands at the station house door, inside the low stone walls. From the well, the raft and the landing stage are about 65 yards to the north, across the ford, with the round mud huts behind them on the far bank. If the road runs on into open marsh with no roofs in sight, you have passed it.

journal_text: At Claywater Station, Livia Varinius told me she raised the station's charge to 2 drakes to pay a mason to re-line the cracked well in stone. Signs-For-The-Cargo told me the landing began charging walkers at the ford. The landing worked this ford before the well was dug. The landing will not haul stone for the station. Signs-For-The-Cargo says a crocodile has taken the landing's clay cut below the ford. The landing will hear terms only from whoever wins back the cut before the rains. I'm to kill the crocodile and bring back the clay basket that lies at the cut. The cut is below the ford on the station bank. From the well, I go about 45 yards west, outside the low stone walls, to where the river swings west under a bare clay bank and the water lies deep and dark. If the bank flattens into reeds, I have gone past it. Signs-For-The-Cargo says Takes-The-Short-Weight can tell what ails the station's water. She lives in the round mud hut on the landing bank, about 30 yards north of the raft. In the morning she sits at the landing's fire, about 50 yards north of the raft.
directions: The clay cut is below the ford on the station bank: from the well, go about 45 yards west, outside the low stone walls, to where the river swings west under a bare clay bank and the water lies deep and dark. If the bank flattens into reeds, you have gone past it. Takes-The-Short-Weight lives in the round mud hut on the landing bank, about 30 yards north of the raft; in the morning she sits at the landing's fire, about 50 yards north of the raft.

journal_text: I killed the crocodile at the clay cut below the ford at Claywater Station and have the landing's clay basket. I'm to put terms to Livia Varinius and to Signs-For-The-Cargo before the rains: one charge of 2 drakes a stop, 1 to each bank, with the landing's clay rammed in behind the cracked lining. Livia Varinius says a mason's lining will mend the well and mud has no place in it. She says the landing would take half a charge for water it never draws. I'm to find out whether the well has cracked before. Takes-The-Short-Weight can taste the station's water if I bring it to her in Livia Varinius's dipper. Signs-For-The-Cargo says the station only wants stone. He will not haul it. Livia Varinius is at the well in the morning, at the counter by the station house door in the afternoon and at the stable at dusk. Signs-For-The-Cargo poles the raft in the morning and is at the drying racks behind it in the afternoon.
directions: Livia Varinius is at the well in the morning, at the counter by the station house door in the afternoon and at the stable at dusk; Signs-For-The-Cargo poles the raft in the morning and is at the drying racks behind it in the afternoon.

journal_text: I brought Livia Varinius and Signs-For-The-Cargo to terms at Claywater Station: one charge of 2 drakes a stop, 1 to each bank. The landing has rammed its clay in behind the cracked lining before the rains. I killed the crocodile at the clay cut and gave the landing back its basket. Livia Varinius will send for no mason. Travellers no longer have a reason to wade below the cut at night. The ferry at the Drowning Gate is free to me from now on.

I found that travellers at Claywater Station paid Livia Varinius at the well and again at the ford. I paid Signs-For-The-Cargo 100 drakes to take no charge from walkers this season, so they pay once, at the well. The well is still cracked.

I found that travellers at Claywater Station paid Livia Varinius at the well and again at the ford. I also found that the well's lining has cracked and been mended every year. To keep that quiet, Livia Varinius has dropped her charge back to the old drake. Signs-For-The-Cargo has dropped the walkers' charge in answer. Livia Varinius will send for no mason. The well is still cracked. The ferry at the Drowning Gate is free to me from now on.
The rains came to Claywater Station before I made terms between Livia Varinius and Signs-For-The-Cargo. The well is still cracked. Travellers still pay at both banks or wade below the ford at night.

Livia Varinius is dead. The well at Claywater Station has no keeper now. The station's charge ended with her. Signs-For-The-Cargo keeps the landing's charge on the ford. The two charges cannot be settled now.
Signs-For-The-Cargo is dead. The raft at Claywater Station has no poler. The landing will make no terms with Livia Varinius and the station while it mourns. Both charges stand.
Mee-Sei, who cooks at the fire stand in Greenspring, told me that guests at the lodge have been falling sick, and that people blame his food. I'm to find out what is making them ill.
directions: The pool lies under the Hist, a few steps from the fire stand; the lodge, where the sick guests lie, faces it across the spring.

journal_text: The guests at the Greenspring lodge sicken from the spring, not from Mee-Sei's food. Only Im-Moro, the spring-keeper, may go into the pool under the Hist. I'm to get into the pool, with her leave or without it at night.
directions: The stone lip is on the lodge side of the pool; the Hist's roots go down into the water on the far side.

journal_text: I have gone into the pool under the Hist at Greenspring. I'm to search the spring's throat between the roots, where the water comes up.

A dead man lies staked in the throat of the spring at Greenspring, his wrists tied with rope, the stake left blank. That is what sickens the guests. I'm to find out who he was and who killed him, before the killer leaves.
directions: The lodge store is the locked room behind Haj-Tei's door; Reeh-Shaal sleeps in the lodge and goes to the stone lip after the lamps are out.

journal_text: The courier who vanished from the Greenspring lodge twelve days ago lies in the spring, and what I have found points to Reeh-Shaal, the guest who says she waits for a boat to Helstrom. I'm to confront her with what I hold, and I need two things to make it stand.

I named Reeh-Shaal before the people of Greenspring as the one who killed the Helstrom courier and staked him in the spring. Im-Moro has had the body raised and given to the Hist, and the root-herald holds Reeh-Shaal for Helstrom.
Reeh-Shaal is dead by my hand at Greenspring. Im-Moro has had the courier's body raised from the spring, and the guests should mend.
I took the sealed packet from Reeh-Shaal at Greenspring and let her go. Nobody there will learn who killed the courier.
I accused Tsono-Ra of the courier's murder at Greenspring, and I was wrong. The village has closed ranks against me, and Reeh-Shaal has taken the boat.
Reeh-Shaal has left Greenspring on the Helstrom boat. Whoever killed the courier in the spring has gone, and the guests are still sick.
At Helstrom's river landing a raft-poler, Okan-Tei, says a beast lives under the pier and has taken a raft. I'm to find what keeps it there.
directions: Okan-Tei stands on the landing below the ship's door, by the second raft.

journal_text: Something under the landing pier keeps the beast there. I'm to search under the pier, from the pier unseen by the crew or by swimming under it.
directions: The pier runs out from the landing into the river; the bait lies at two points by the pilings under it. The crew watch the pier by day.

journal_text: Someone has been dumping fish offal under the pier, night after night, and it drew the beast in. It lairs by the pilings. I'm to kill it under the pier, or lure it into the open shallows with the bait and kill it there.
directions: The lair is in the shallows by the pilings under the pier. The open shallows lie south of the pier's end.

journal_text: The beast is dead. Wuleen-Sei of the landing crew laid the bait to scare the boat captain's trade off the river. I'm to put it to the boat captain in Helstrom, or put it to Wuleen-Sei and take her price to keep quiet.
directions: Wuleen-Sei stands on the landing by the first raft. The boat captain keeps her boat at Helstrom's river stair, up the way from the landing past the gate.

journal_text: I told the boat captain that the landing crew baited the pier and drew the beast in. She paid me for it, and the crew have lost their trade on the river to her.
Wuleen-Sei paid me to keep the bait to myself. The crew keep their trade, and the boat captain still thinks the river took her customers.
At Helstrom's basin gate Haj-Wan says her kin Sei-Wan walked out into the basin alone four hours ago, and the levy warden will not follow. Their custom does not bind me.
directions: Haj-Wan waits inside the gate, beside the levy warden.

journal_text: Sei-Wan cut reeds to mark his way east from the gate. I'm to follow the cut reeds through the basin's water and mud to wherever he stopped.
directions: Out of the gate, the cut reeds run east through the shallows, two cells along, to a reed shelter.

journal_text: Sei-Wan is alive in the reed shelter, and a crocodile keeps him there. I'm to kill it. If he does not see me do it, his walk-out is still his own.
directions: The shelter stands in the water at the end of the cut reeds; the crocodile circles it.

journal_text: The crocodile is dead. I can slip back to the gate without Sei-Wan seeing me and let him walk home alone, or talk to him and bring him back myself.
directions: Sei-Wan is in the reed shelter; the gate is back west along the cut reeds.

journal_text: Sei-Wan walked back through the gate alone, and his walk-out is his own. Haj-Wan knows who killed the crocodile and gave me what she had.
I brought Sei-Wan back through the gate. He is alive, but the walk-out is not his, and he will not look at me. Haj-Wan thanked me.

I came to in the hold of a broker's barge at Lilmoth's dock, among an Owing gang. Wuleen-Sei, the overseer, is reading the roll aloud, each name, the months owed and the months added for food, and my line is blank. I'm to answer her when she reaches it, then follow Wuleen-Sei up the plank, past Buys-The-Months, the broker on the pier, and north and west along the shore path to the families' camp at the edge of Hereguard Plantation, to the camp's fire.
directions: The hold is the barge's one room below the deck; its door leads up to the plank and the pier of Lilmoth's dock. From the plank at Lilmoth's dock the shore path runs north and west along the water, past the first of the rice dikes; the camp is the cluster of huts on the reed bank at the paddy edge, where the path meets the reeds. The fire is in the middle of the camp; the hatching shed stands beside the cutting at the camp's far end.

journal_text: As Wuleen-Sei read the roll at the camp's fire, in sight of the families' Hist cutting and the shed that holds their clutch, naming Sal-Sei, keeper of the clutch, and Deesh-Duun aloud, a tall Argonian woman with a knotted cord at her wrist came in off the water with two of her people, killed Mee-Tuja, the quiet man who walked with us, at the fire, took his satchel and looked at me, and left. In the struggle his strap with a brass tag was torn off and fell through the burnt boards into the deep water. The roll went into the fire. Her people are at the cutting and the huts are burning. Sal-Sei is at the shed and Deesh-Duun is hiding from the blades in the huts. I'm to reach one of them; I cannot reach both.
directions: The shed is at the camp's far end beside the cutting; the cell's two cutters stand between the fire and the shed. The burning huts stand over the deep water under the plank boards and are entered only from the water.

journal_text: I ran for the hatching shed at the camp on Hereguard Plantation's paddy edge. Two of the woman's people have cut the roots that tie the cutting to the clutch, and Sal-Sei is on the ground beside the eggs. Behind me the huts have fallen in where Deesh-Duun was. I'm to drive the cutters off, or hide in the reeds until they leave, and get Sal-Sei out through the reeds to the shore.
directions: From the shed the reeds run south to the shore below the camp, the way the families fish at night; keep the burning huts on the left hand.

journal_text: I went into the burning huts at the camp on Hereguard Plantation's paddy edge and pulled Deesh-Duun out through the deep water under the plank boards. She saw the woman with the knotted cord as closely as I did. From the water I saw the cutters leave the shed, and Sal-Sei did not come out. I'm to bring Deesh-Duun round the burning end of the camp to the shore.
directions: The shore is south of the huts; keep under the plank boards and the burning end of the camp stays on the left hand.

journal_text: I got out of the burning camp on Hereguard Plantation's paddy edge with Sal-Sei, the clutch-keeper. The eggs under the cut roots are dead and the cutting has withdrawn. The roll burned in the fire, so nobody can say what I owe, and nobody can say what I do not.

I got out of the burning camp on Hereguard Plantation's paddy edge with Deesh-Duun, who saw the woman with the knotted cord as closely as I did. The roll burned in the fire, so nobody can say what I owe.
I got out of the burning camp on Hereguard Plantation's paddy edge alone. Sal-Sei and Deesh-Duun are dead. The roll burned in the fire, so nobody can say what I owe.

At dawn the camp on Hereguard Plantation's paddy edge is a ruin and I came out of the fire burnt. Two strangers, who say a friend of the courier's sent them, are taking off the hurt. Sap the cutters spilled lies on the shed floor, and the courier Mee-Tuja's brass tag fell through the burnt plank boards at the fire into the deep water. I could taste the sap and take a phial of it, or dive for the tag, before the boat goes.
directions: The shed stands beside the withdrawn cutting at the camp's far end. The burnt plank boards lie at the camp's fire over the deep water; the courier's strap and tag lie on the bottom straight below them, one breath down.

journal_text: The strangers took the hurt to a house in Lilmoth that a fish-trader, Salts-The-Catch, keeps. In the back room, behind a screen, a woman who calls herself Nesh-Deeka sits by the mats, and Ties-The-Loose-Plank lies on one of them. Nesh-Deeka is of the Veiled Reed. The roll burnt at the camp, so nobody can show what I owe or that I was on it, and almost no one knows my face. I'm to tell her what I saw, and get Ties to tell it too, then rest in the house until night on a mat in the back room.
directions: The house has no mark; the back room is past the front room's table, behind the screen, the mats beside it. Sleep or wait on a mat there until night.

journal_text: I rested in the house in Lilmoth until night with the camp's sap still on my tongue, and dreamed. I stood in fog among a ring of trees whose roots climbed up and up, and at the top was a gap like a door that nobody has built. A dry voice spoke that I could not place. I'm to climb the root ledges to the door at the top.
directions: The roots of the ring climb from the fog to the door-gap at the top.

journal_text: I climbed to the door in the dream and woke in the house in Lilmoth. I have taken the Veiled Reed's oath: Nesh-Deeka says no one will come asking what I owe, the house's door is open to me, and she put the first of a stipend in my hand.
I climbed to the door in the dream and woke in the house in Lilmoth. I have taken no oath. The house's door is not mine, but the Reed will send for me when it has work, and pay for it.

The Reed sent me east of Lilmoth to Low-Reed Village, where the Hist has turned its face. The root-herald, on the platform at the Hist's foot, does not like strangers from Lilmoth. I'm to talk her round, or bring her a gift, for leave to see the tree.
directions: The village lies east of Lilmoth along the reed paths, its jetty on the west side; the root-herald keeps the platform at the Hist's foot.

journal_text: The tending-ground at Low-Reed Village is closed, the Hist dark and its leaves shut, and the uxith is dark, as it was at the camp. The village says the leeches did it. I'm to go down into the water under the stilts, to the tree's lowest root, and see for myself.
directions: The roots run down from the tending-ground into the water under the stilts; the cut root is the lowest.

journal_text: A root of the Hist was cut at the ring and sealed with black gum, and the leeches only came to the weeping sap. Pays-Late, the tree-minder, whom the village blames, goes down to wash it after dark. I'm to watch him there unseen at night, or ask the egg-tender at the uxith by day, and find out who cut it.
directions: Pays-Late goes down to the cut root after dark; the egg-tender keeps the uxith by day.

journal_text: Strangers came and went by the north reeds. I'm to swim the leech water north of the village, follow the bent reeds to the strangers' camp on the dry rise, take the jars of the Hist's sap, and pour them back at the cut root under the stilts.
directions: The leech water lies north of the village where the reeds open; past it the reed stems are bent toward a dry rise two cells out. The cut root is under the stilts.

journal_text: I poured the jars back at the cut root and left Pays-Late's knife with them, where he found it. The village knows now that it was strangers' work and not his keeping. The Hist's light is coming back, low and slow. The village has taken me in.
The cell cut a Hist's root at Low-Reed Village for its sap, and I saw the cut. I'm to take what I found back to Nesh-Deeka at the fish-trader's house in Lilmoth, which is the Reed's.
directions: The Reed's house is the fish-trader's, Salts-The-Catch's, on the stilts of Lilmoth's channel; its back room is behind the screen.

journal_text: The Reed wants the tree-minders and Nisswo of Helstrom to hear what a cut Hist looks like, from someone the Reed can deny; it sends no escort. I'm to take the coast ship at Lilmoth's stop: one of its doors opens on Helstrom's river landing. From the landing I'm to follow the marsh way inland, root and shallows, to its far bend.
directions: The coast ship lies at Lilmoth's stop on the east side. Go in by its door at the stop (0AA837, the pair of 0AA664) and through the ship to the door that opens on the river landing (23D496, the pair of 0830A8 on the landing, where BM&V's map marker reads Helstrom); that door is found by its place in the ship, measured at build. The inner door joins the ship's two sections; where it stands is measured at build. From the landing the way runs inland, root and shallows; the far bend is where it turns toward the city.

journal_text: At the way's far bend two giant wasps, each the size of a pony, nest over the Heart-Mud, and the way runs past them on the root. A drowned channel runs under the root. I'm to kill the wasps, or swim the channel under them unseen, and go on past the levy's gate to the grove behind the Hall of the Scalded Throne.
directions: The far bend is where the way turns toward the city; the nest hangs over the Heart-Mud by the root, and the drowned channel opens under the root on the landing side. Past the bend the way runs to the gate soldier at the city's edge. The grove is behind the Hall of the Scalded Throne, by the first street.

journal_text: Behind the hall Kaska-Meen keeps her watch in the grove, and at the root's foot a Nisswo, Ei-Tuja, argues with her over what a silent Hist means. Neither has seen a cut root. I saw one. I'm to tell one of them that a Hist gone silent and a Hist cut at the root are two things, and the clutch died of the cut. The hall of the Scalded Throne by the first street holds a plain seat of root and reed, with no dais, swept with a broom, and the city sells in the room before it.
directions: The Hall of the Scalded Throne is the low-roofed house by the first street, on the left as the way comes in from the gate; its inner room holds the seat and its outer room the merchants. The grove is the stand of root behind the hall: Ei-Tuja stands at the root's foot and Kaska-Meen sits at her watch by the young Hist.

journal_text: In the grove I told Kaska-Meen what I saw at Low-Reed Village: that a Hist gone silent and a Hist cut at the root are two things, and the clutch died of the cut. She heard me out and will carry it to the interior's tree-minders. The Reed is not named in Helstrom.

At the root's foot I told Ei-Tuja what I saw at Low-Reed Village: that a Hist gone silent and a Hist cut at the root are two things, and the clutch died of the cut. He gave his reading freely, as the Nisswo do, and will carry it to the villages he preaches in. The Reed is not named in Helstrom.

Root-Herald Ixo-Vaal of Greenspring asked me, for the Many-Root Conclave, to find out why the village's Hist is sickening. The village blames the salt works upstream. I'm to test the water before I believe them.
directions: The fork lies a short walk upstream of the river landing; the herald's house, with the salt sack at its door, faces the Hist.

journal_text: The salt in Greenspring's spring is not coming down the river. The couriers say the Hist's roots run into the flooded galleries of the Drowned Stair. I'm to go down and take water at each landing.
directions: From Greenspring take the road to the Gate-Side Camp outside Helstrom's gate; the guides there show the stair's mouth, where the deep water starts.

journal_text: The water in the Drowned Stair grows saltier the deeper I go. I'm to reach the deepest chamber, beyond one breath, and see where the salt comes in.

Deep in the Drowned Stair, a channel has been cut by hand into a brine seam, and the floods push the brine into Greenspring's roots. The cut is old. I'm to learn who made it, and Vees-Wai, the tree-minder, reads the old stakes.

Greenspring's founders cut the channel to kill a rival grove downstream, and their deed is killing their own Hist. Ixo-Vaal has called the office-holders to the Hist. I'm to put what I found before them and argue for a cure, and for whether the founders are named.
The office-holders of Greenspring sealed the founders' cut and named the deed at the Hist. The tree should mend, and Greenspring now owes the people of the dead grove an answer.
The office-holders of Greenspring sealed the founders' cut and agreed to say nothing of who made it. The tree should mend.
Greenspring chose to reopen the founders' cut downstream. Their Hist is spared, and the dead grove's land will flood with brine again.

On Soulrest's dock S'Tabi, the Khajiit caravan factor, told me to see Deep-In-Her-Cups in the back room of the house on the dock if I wanted work of the quiet kind. I'm to go through the house's one open door and find her in the back room.
directions: The house is the long one at the east end of Soulrest's dock; of its doors only one opens (120E93), and the back room is through the inner door (0E971F).

journal_text: Deep-In-Her-Cups, who keeps the Chapter's desk at Soulrest, wants to see how I work. Keeps-What-Floats, a dock thief, took a necklace of polished blue jaspers from another thief, and it must come back with no harm done to him. I'm to follow him on the dock and boardwalk without being seen and find where he drinks and where he sleeps.
directions: He walks the dock and the boardwalk west of the house by day; in the evening he drinks by the water at the boardwalk's end with Sits-By-The-Water, and he sleeps under the awning of the boardwalk beyond it.

journal_text: Keeps-What-Floats, who took the necklace of blue jaspers, carries it on the dock by day and leaves it in his bedroll under the boardwalk awning while he drinks in the evening. I'm to get the necklace back without hurting him, by lifting it off him, taking it from his bedroll, or talking him out of it, and bring it to Deep-In-Her-Cups in the back room.
directions: By day he is on the dock west of the house; in the evening his bedroll lies under the boardwalk awning while he drinks at the boardwalk's end. The house's back room is behind its one open door.

journal_text: I brought the necklace of blue jaspers back to Deep-In-Her-Cups at Soulrest, and Keeps-What-Floats came to no harm. She paid me and gave me three lockpicks. The Chapter's way down is a locked trapdoor two squares north of Pusbottom in Lilmoth. I'm to take the coast ship from Soulrest's dock to Lilmoth, open the trapdoor and go down to the Chapter.
directions: The coast ship's door is on Soulrest's dock (039827); inside, the door at Lilmoth's stop (0AA837) opens on Lilmoth's east side (0AA664). Pusbottom lies west of the stop, by the canals; the trapdoor (16BF7F) is in the ground two squares north of it.

journal_text: I brought the necklace of blue jaspers back to Deep-In-Her-Cups at Soulrest, but Keeps-What-Floats is dead. She paid me nothing, and said the Chapter wanted the necklace without a body, but she gave me three lockpicks and sent me on. The Chapter's way down is a locked trapdoor two squares north of Pusbottom in Lilmoth. I'm to take the coast ship from Soulrest's dock to Lilmoth, open the trapdoor and go down to the Chapter.
directions: The coast ship's door is on Soulrest's dock (039827); inside, the door at Lilmoth's stop (0AA837) opens on Lilmoth's east side (0AA664). Pusbottom lies west of the stop, by the canals; the trapdoor (16BF7F) is in the ground two squares north of it.

journal_text: I got the necklace of blue jaspers back from Keeps-What-Floats at Soulrest without hurting him, and Deep-In-Her-Cups paid me. I opened the trapdoor north of Pusbottom with my own hand and went down to the Chapter, and Bent-Spine took me in as a Lookout.

I got the necklace of blue jaspers back at Soulrest, but Keeps-What-Floats died for it, and Deep-In-Her-Cups paid me nothing. I opened the trapdoor north of Pusbottom with my own hand and went down to the Chapter, and Bent-Spine took me in as a Lookout.
I'm in the Night-Reed Chapter now, under Pusbottom in Lilmoth. I'm to speak to Bent-Spine, the Chapter's fence, about the work he has.
directions: Bent-Spine keeps to the Chapter's inner room, past the foot of the trapdoor's ladder.

journal_text: Bent-Spine, the Chapter's fence, wants the lockbox of a merchant whose stilt house fell into the Pusbottom canal; it lies locked on the canal floor beside the house, and ripper eels hunt the water. Three clients on the canal front want it. I'm to talk to each of them, Neeta-Haj, Okan-Tei and Dar-Zeel, and get out of each what they claim the box holds for them.
directions: Climb the trapdoor's ladder out of the Chapter and go two squares south to Pusbottom; the fallen house lies in the canal there, and the three clients wait on the canal front above it.

journal_text: Neeta-Haj says the bone figurine in the lockbox was carved for her clutch, Okan-Tei that the charm was only pledged and never sold, and Dar-Zeel that the beads are old family work. The box lies locked on the floor of the Pusbottom canal beside the fallen stilt house, and ripper eels hunt the water. I'm to dive to it, slip past the eels, pick its lock, take the figurine, the charm and the beads, and swim out.
directions: The fallen house lies on its side on the canal floor below the canal front; the lockbox is in the open beside it.

journal_text: I brought up the figurine, the charm and the beads from the lockbox in the Pusbottom canal, and each gives a client the lie. The figurine is worn smooth by many years of handling, older than any clutch of Neeta-Haj's; the charm is in a new silver mount the merchant put on it, so Okan-Tei sold it; the beads are Kothringi glass from the old cairns, no family work of Dar-Zeel's. I'm to settle it on the canal front, by handing all three things to one client, or by talking each client into buying back their own pledge.
directions: The three clients wait on the canal front above the fallen house.

journal_text: I brought up the lockbox's figurine, charm and beads from the Pusbottom canal, past the ripper eels, and gave all three to one of the clients on the canal front, who paid me for them. The other two will not forget it.

I brought up the lockbox's figurine, charm and beads from the Pusbottom canal, past the ripper eels, and sold each back to the client who had lied about it, at the price the box showed. Neeta-Haj, Okan-Tei and Dar-Zeel paid, and none of them will greet me kindly again.
